description: PySeidon is a data-driven, extendable simulator of maritime port operations, written in Python with an entity-component-system design. It simulates vessels, tugboats and pilots together with berths, anchorages and tug and pilot rendezvous and storage locations, so that scenarios such as a new anchorage, a different number of tugs or pilots, or a different priority order by ship class can be tested against key performance indicators; it can also inject anomalies (random berth inspections, tugboat malfunctions, unusual vessel speeds) to generate datasets that do not exist. It was developed at Maastricht University and presented at the 13th International Conference on Computer Modeling and Simulation in June 2021. It is location independent and works at the scale of a single port: any port can be simulated when its input data are available, with minimal code changes. The code is free on GitHub with documentation, and companion GitLab repositories provide AIS analysis and visualisation tools. Caveats: the repository has no licence file, so reuse rights are unclear, there are no tagged releases and the last commit was in September 2024. PySeidon supports capacity planning, agent-based and resilience studies of port operations and the generation of synthetic AIS-like data, and relates to AIS vessel traffic data such as the Marine Cadastre series catalogued here.
